chunks: 1833 - Jabir narrated from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said:

“The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله would, when he saw the crescent of the month of Ramadan, face the qiblah with his face, then say: ‘O Allah, let it appear over us with security, faith, safety, Islam, all-encompassing well-being, abundant provision, warding off illnesses, recitation of the Qur’an, and help in salat (prayer) and sawm (fasting). O Allah, keep us safe for the month of Ramadan, keep it safe for us, and receive it from us until the month of Ramadan comes to an end while You have forgiven us.’”

Then he would turn his face to the people and say: ‘O gathering of people, when the crescent of the month of Ramadan rises, the rebellious devils are chained, the gates of heaven, the gates of the gardens, and the gates of mercy are opened, and the gates of the Fire are closed. Supplication is answered, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has at every breaking of the fast those whom He frees from the Fire. And a caller calls out every night: Is there any repentant one? Is there any asker? Is there any seeker of forgiveness? O Allah, give every spender a replacement, and give every withholder loss. Until, when the crescent of Shawwal rises, the believers are called: Go early to your rewards, for it is the Day of Reward.’
Then Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said: ‘Indeed, by the One in whose hand is my soul, it is not a reward of dinars and dirhams.’

key_terms.الصِّيَامِ: sawm (fasting), especially the fast of Ramadan
key_terms.الْأَسْقَامِ: illnesses and ailments from which protection is sought
key_terms.تِلَاوَةِ الْقُرْآنِ: the recitation of the Qur’an as a devotional act
key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: the blessed month of fasting, mercy, and forgiveness
key_terms.عُتَقَاءُ: those set free by Allah from the Fire
key_terms.هِلَالِ: the new crescent marking the beginning of the lunar month

ai.seo_question: What did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله say when the crescent of Ramadan was seen, and what virtues does Ramadan bring?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the supplication of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله upon sighting the crescent of Ramadan and the immense spiritual openings associated with the month. It highlights Ramadan as a time of mercy, answered du'a, forgiveness, liberation from the Fire, and divine reward that surpasses worldly wealth.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1833 - It is narrated by Jabir from Abu Ja‘far (Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as)), who said:
"Whenever the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) saw the crescent of the Month of Ramadan, he would face the Qiblah and say:
'O Allah (swt), let this crescent appear over us with security, faith, peace, and submission, along with encompassing wellness, ample sustenance, protection from ailments, recitation of the Qur’an, and assistance in prayer and fasting. O Allah (swt), safeguard us for the Month of Ramadan, safeguard it for us, and accept it from us until the Month of Ramadan concludes, and You have forgiven us.'
Then he would turn to the people and say:
'O people, when the crescent of Month of Ramadan rises, the rebellious devils are chained, the gates of the heavens, Paradise, and mercy are opened, and the gates of Hell are closed. Supplications are answered, and Allah (swt), the Blessed and Exalted, frees people from the Fire every night at the time of breaking the fast. A caller announces every night: "Is there anyone who seeks repentance? Is there anyone who asks for something? Is there anyone seeking forgiveness?" O Allah (swt), grant every giver compensation, and bring destruction upon every miser.'
When the crescent of Shawwal appears, it is announced to the believers: "Go forth to your rewards, for this is the Day of Reward."'
Then Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said:
'By the One in whose hand is my soul, the rewards are not in dinars or dirhams.'"
